It has transformed human understanding and given us the tools to improve health, feed the world, and explore the cosmos. "How Your Body Works" is a remarkable work that brings this subject to life for readers aged 7-12. Your body is made of about 37 trillion cells, each doing a special job. The heart beats 100,000 times a day, pumping blood through 96,000 km of blood vessels. The brain has 86 billion neurons that communicate through electrical signals. Bones protect organs and make blood cells, while muscles work in pairs — one contracts while the other relaxes to move your limbs. This book has earned its place as an essential read precisely because it combines deep knowledge with compelling writing, making complex ideas accessible without sacrificing their richness or accuracy. Understanding the subject it covers is valuable not only for academic success but for developing the intellectual tools needed to navigate an increasingly complex world.

The field of science is one of the most important areas of human knowledge, and "How Your Body Works" provides an outstanding introduction to its core ideas. Engaging seriously with this subject helps develop critical thinking, careful reasoning, and the habit of basing conclusions on evidence rather than assumption or tradition. Students who study science learn to ask better questions, evaluate competing claims, and make more informed decisions -- skills that are invaluable in every area of life, from personal choices to professional careers to participation in democratic society. The ideas explored in this book are relevant not only to examinations but to the real challenges facing individuals and communities in the twenty-first century.
